limitations: Host macOS arm64 only; neither iOS Simulator nor Android/device ABI or public-call parity evidence.
Rust LLVM 22 and Apple clang 17 are different compiler implementations. O3/release and one host do not establish matched compiler/target/allocator settings; actual versions/options are recorded.

Original host-only loaders retained. C++ does not reserve metadata, bypasses generated ParityTree(vector) copy constructor, and passes lvalues to generated node constructors. This does not reproduce Nitro JSIConverter allocator history.

Rust JSON decode followed by postcard round-trip creates extra temporary allocations absent from native dispatch. Its final input capacities are inferred resident capacities solely because parity_store moves the same owned tree without transforming its fields.

C++ final resident observation includes repeated optional copy assignment across the ordered fixtures, including balanced8191 then wide1025. Resident is never reconstructed or shrunk to force capacity equality.
No JSI/FFI/conversion/setup is inside the measured interval. The C++ handwritten class shim omits Nitro/JSI inheritance and virtual surface, so this is not exact native ABI or heap-history evidence.

Timing includes 16 calls, result consumption/checksum, and result destruction. Rust adds black_box on query and result; C++ consumes an externally compiled result with separate translation units and -fno-lto. Barriers differ.

Rust default release LTO=false permits compiler-local thin LTO with default multiple codegen units; C++ explicitly disables LTO. Neither driver uses explicit target-cpu/features overrides unless captured in the environment/compiler invocation.

The non-timed probes preserve exact original initialization and child-push expressions; trace-vector allocations and observer branches perturb allocator activity, so they establish growth policy, not timing or cache causality.
Rust probe reads final input before move outside lock; C++ probe reads final resident under mutex. These observations do not measure identical lock/setup paths.
Map bucket count is meaningful for libc++ unordered_map only. Rust BTreeMap has no public bucket count; heap bytes and allocation counts remain unmeasured.
Fixture loader format is restricted to printable ASCII by the TypeScript exporter. std::quoted is not a general JSON Unicode/control-escape decoder.

Five launch means per framework are descriptive. Ratio is arithmetic mean(Rust launch means) / arithmetic mean(C++ launch means). No confidence interval, public-v2 acceptance threshold, statistical equality, regression, or causal layout claim is inferred.
Inspection is a separate process launch from timing. Actual C++ resident capacities describe deterministic setup in inspection; allocator placement of later timing processes is not directly observed.

# Task 3 core harness fix1 review

2026-09-16. Scoped read-only re-review of the four P2 findings in `task-3-core-review.md`, the new `scripts/nitro-core-diagnostic/` sources, updated Rust example, source instrumentation diff, legacy supplement/snapshots, and the parent's completed `core-dfs-next` command/inspection/build/receipt evidence. No build, test, benchmark, or device call was run by this reviewer. Only this report was written.

**Verdict: the four original review findings are addressed for the explicitly limited host diagnostic. No new blocking correctness/fairness issue found in the reviewed scope. A new timing run is not required to close these review findings.** This does not declare phone/public parity, matched compiler backends, allocator equivalence or a causal performance explanation.

## Finding disposition

| Original finding | Disposition | Evidence and remaining boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Input capacity mislabeled as resident capacity | Addressed | Both drivers label input values explicitly. The C++ diagnostic getter reads the actual final resident under its original mutex after the three replacements, preserving a single object across all four shapes. Rust explicitly labels final-input capacities as inferred from the unchanged move into Resident; it does not pretend to use a getter. New inspection is not retroactively assigned to old timing-process heap state. |
| Incomplete source/build/run provenance | Addressed prospectively, historical gaps disclosed | Versioned v2 runner freezes source/generated/input hashes; preserves command argv/cwd/time/exit/stdout/stderr hashes; records compiler/default-target information and build options; copies/hashes actual binaries. The parent build commands and both inspect commands have exit 0. Legacy supplement preserves original binary/raw hashes and labels historical commands/status as parent-reported, with incomplete contemporaneous environment/source evidence retained as a limitation. |
| Loader differs from actual Nitro conversion | Addressed by narrowed claim | The original loaders remain, and README/receipt limitations identify Nitro reserve/constructor/lvalue-copy differences and Rust JSON/postcard temporary allocation history. All fields of each final tree now compare against actual TypeScript exports, with documented absent-note/integral-number normalization. Same semantic input is established separately from heap/construction equivalence. |
| Missing stack growth evidence | Addressed | Inspection-only copied search probes retain the exact original initialization, traversal and child-push expressions. Preparation restores and byte-compares only the whitelisted observer/signature/braces changes; the recorded instrumentation diff agrees. Capacity sequences, growth counts, max-live values and results are present and validated in the parent's inspection receipt. Timed production search bodies remain unchanged. |

## Concrete observations in the new receipt

- The fixed fixture order is balanced255, balanced1023, balanced8191, wide1025. C++ wide1025 retains **node capacity 8191**, child-capacity sum **2050**, and **513 empty child vectors with allocations**. Rust's final restored wide input, moved unchanged into resident, has **node capacity 1025**, child-capacity sum **1024**, and no allocated empty children. The new labels correctly distinguish direct observation from move-based inference.
- Rust stack sequences start `1,4,8`; C++ starts `1,2,4,8`. Post-initial growth counts for balanced255/1023/8191/wide1025 are respectively **Rust 2/3/3/9** and **C++ 3/4/4/10**. Both max-live sequences are **8/10/13/1024**. These are inspection-probe capacity-policy observations, not allocator latency or total allocation-byte measurements.
- The full-tree canonical digests agree across frameworks for all four fixtures. `run.py` compares all actual reconstructed fields with TypeScript-exported expected trees before assigning the canonical digest. The raw full trees remain available; compact receipts do not replace their evidence.
- Current host node sizes remain Rust **128 bytes**, C++ **152 bytes**, alignment 8; search sizes are 48. Heap allocations and device layouts are not inferred from these numbers.

## Source and lifetime checks

Inspection branches run before any timer and in separate processes. Rust's inspection-only tree clone and JSON observation allocations do not run in timing mode. C++ introspection holds the original mutex and does not clear or shrink resident state. Both timing loops retain the real resident call and per-iteration result consumption/destruction; C++ still releases its loader tree after storage. The Rust query/result black-box difference and C++ separate-translation-unit surface are documented. The handwritten C++ class ABI and loader construction history remain intentionally different from the app.

The whitelisted Rust/C++ probes preserve original stack initialization and push expressions. Observer allocations can perturb allocator activity, so they establish capacity sequences rather than timing/cache effects; the documentation states this. TypeScript export restricts string content to printable ASCII, matching the current custom quoted-text loader's supported scope.

The new build record uses ordinary Rust release and C++ O3 with explicit C++ `-fno-lto`; it correctly discloses Rust local thin-LTO/default CPU and compiler-backend differences instead of claiming a perfectly matched toolchain. Source hashes and commands make this a reproducible host recipe within those disclosed constraints.

## Completion boundary

The reviewed new `receipt.json` has **`timing: null`**. Its command history ends with successful non-timed Rust/C++ inspection. The existing four legacy point ratios remain exploratory observations of the original host harness; the new observations do not authenticate the earlier processes' exact capacities/addresses and do not prove why a ratio occurred. A separately identified timing run is available if the parent later needs one, but rerunning it would not be necessary merely to close these four review findings.

The fixer's report describes build/inspection as pending at its pre-handoff point. The parent's later successful command logs and inspection receipt, reviewed here, supply that missing execution evidence. No source changes or additional benchmark request result from this review.
